order: Fix continuous-integration failures on macOS and Windows that appeared following the structural sweep guard change. Git records canonical worktree paths, but a live checkout's own handle may be spelled through a symlink or a short alias path, so a lexical comparison inside the sweep's live-set exemption misses the match and the sweep deletes a live checkout mid-verification. The path-normalization function looks up real paths first, falling back to a lexical comparison only for paths that are already gone — not for a path still on disk. Pin a regression using an aliased temporary-root reproducer, such as a junction or symlink, that must fail on every platform without the fix, skipping cleanly where links cannot be created. Confine the fix to the normalization function and the live-set comparison; the sweep's other classification logic does not change.
claims: The live-set exemption's path comparison now looks up real paths, falling back lexically only for paths already gone, which fixes the macOS and Windows continuous-integration failures caused by a canonical-versus-aliased path mismatch. A regression was pinned using an aliased temporary-root reproducer, built from a junction or symlink, that fails on every platform without the fix; the diff stat shows 25 lines added to the verifier test suite and 11 to the checkout module, with no other files touched.
